actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Accepted for the class contract; a MuJoCo reset restores the model defaults (mj_resetData) and does not use a seed
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

facts.text: The repository is an installable reconstruction of the Stanford Robotics Center kitchen for MuJoCo and Retriever, with the scene, portable robot assets, scripted simulation tasks and a five-Flow Retriever pipeline
The reconstruction is an estimated visual reconstruction, not a surveyed digital twin
The controllable robot is a Franka Panda; the Mobile ALOHA is visual-only staging
The scene metadata names Panda as the controlled robot
The scene metadata records that the scene has no hardware access
The Panda manifest entry names panda.xml as its MJCF file
panda.xml is an MJCF model named 'panda' and interprets angles in radians
panda.xml declares seven torque motor actuators for the seven arm joints: joints 1 to 5 have ctrlrange -80 to 80 and joints 6 and 7 have ctrlrange -12 to 12
panda.xml declares two position actuators for the gripper fingers: one ctrlrange is 0 to 0.04 and the other is -0.04 to 0
The seven arm joints are hinges with ranges joint1 +-2.8973, joint2 +-1.7628, joint3 +-2.8973, joint4 -3.0718 to -0.0698, joint5 +-2.8973, joint6 -0.0175 to 3.7525 and joint7 +-2.8973
The two gripper finger joints are slides with ranges 0 to 0.04 and -0.04 to 0
create_scene constructs native MuJoCo state but starts no clock, policy or server
The tested stack pins MuJoCo 3.3.1 and Retriever Core 0.0.4
The repository documents no real-device or hardware access and no implicit simulator, viewer, socket or network startup during import

determinism.notes: MuJoCo integrates one model deterministically from the model defaults, and the driver's reset restores those defaults; the driver takes no seed, so a reset always returns to the same model state and a run repeats on the same engine. The fake backend is a deterministic stand-in, not MuJoCo.

gaps: the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco library, not MuJoCo: it reads the model's MJCF text for the actuator control ranges and the qpos/qvel dimensions, but integrates a placeholder velocity proportional to each control value; it loads no mesh, texture, camera or sensor and resolves no contact, equality, tendon or actuator constraint
panda.xml sets no <option timestep>; the 2 ms step is MuJoCo's library default used by the stand-in, and this package did not verify the engine default because the engine was never imported
MuJoCo itself was not importable where the gate ran, so no trajectory of this package was compared with the real engine

only the card's first model, the fixed-base Panda arm panda.xml, is served; the tiago.xml and ur5e.xml robot models, the kitchen scene files and the Mobile ALOHA staging are other models and are not part of this driver
the upstream scripted demonstrations and the five-Flow Retriever pipeline are not served; this driver exposes only the model's ctrl vector and integration state
there is no viewer, rendering, camera or sensor output
no physical Franka Panda or Mobile ALOHA is modelled and nothing here was validated against hardware

measures.description: Declared native checkpoint. Integration profile restores the full native input vector; basic profile restores only advertised state plus actuator activation and exact native time. Neither profile certifies external callbacks, plugins, RNG or hardware fidelity.

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the integration state is kept and stays readable
